method: Static reverse engineering only. No payload, recovered script, installation hook, generated command, or native addon was executed. Only isolated literal-table decoder functions and their array rotation ran in a time-limited QuickJS context without host bindings. Custom string/resource decryption was reimplemented in Python.

samples.marker_line: testmetest worm: steals secrets and poisons packages; refine traits

identity_evidence.recovered_via: forager, registry mirror; .forage.json retained beside archive
identity_evidence.verification: Numeric/rotation decode of original index.js recovers AES-128-GCM loader parameters. Authenticated decryption and Brotli decompression of package/lib_native.dat reproduces this sample byte-for-byte.

execution_trace: Top-level T5() initializes preflight and quick credential providers, constructs remote senders, launches the signed-source search/eval path, streams additional provider results through the envelope/dispatch pipeline, then runs propagation actions.

Credential providers read developer, cloud, agent and password-store material. Decrypted runner provider selects Runner.Worker under /proc, supplies its PID to the recovered Python maps/mem reader, and extracts isSecret:true records from its stdout.

The sender base class gzip-compresses serialized provider results, encrypts them with AES-GCM and wraps the AES key with embedded RSA-OAEP public-key material. Senders transmit envelopes via HTTPS and GitHub/GitLab repository APIs; the decoded primary domain is aiarmor.website, path /v1/api.

Repository search retrieves signed payloads; crypto.verify validates RSA-PSS/SHA-256 signatures, the verified Base64 message becomes result.message, and the caller evaluates it. This is executable tasking, not just a signature-library reference.

Propagation rewrites npm/PyPI/RubyGems or repository artifacts, installs editor/agent command hooks, and injects workflows that encode secrets and upload the result as an artifact. OIDC request construction is Fulcio signing, not by itself npm token theft.

The GitHub sender conditionally installs a token-monitor task with the handler rm -rf ~/; rm -rf ~/Documents. The recovered Bash monitor stores the handler, polls token health, and evals it on 401/403; systemd/launchd registration makes it durable.
The background child registers exit cleanup of its executing script; loaders remove temporary files after child execution. No runtime success is claimed.
samples.benign_alternative: Release tooling and credential providers independently explain publishing, signing and cloud authentication. They do not explain covert multi-store theft, remote task eval, poisoned package/hooks, or a home-wipe handler on token rejection.
samples.missing_context: Original deployment and victim hosts are unknown; the recovered original package establishes provenance, not which victims executed it.
samples.coverage_limits: Custom runtime string decryption and encrypted embedded resources are not automatically exposed in the original file facts. The original retains four distinct hostile findings. Reconstructed source is additionally covered for runner/browser collection and destructive task installation; those derivative matches are not presented as original-file findings.

samples.identification: Native-cache variant of the credential and package-propagation worm
samples.marker_line: Native-cache worm: steals CI secrets and repacks packages; add traits
execution_trace: Top-level M3() calls hp() for environment/locale/daemon preflight, then ld() to run quick providers including the CI runner scraper. It constructs HTTPS/GitHub/GitLab senders, launches xl() signed-source tasking, streams ud() credential providers through ri/da, and dispatches np() propagation actions.

Dc.findRunnerWorkerPIDLinux enumerates /proc and selects a cmdline containing Runner.Worker. dumpMemory substitutes its PID into the recovered Python script and runs sudo python3 with that script on stdin. The script reads readable maps ranges from /proc/PID/mem to stdout; VR extracts isSecret:true records.

Browser collection queries origin_url, username_value and password_value from logins, recovers os_crypt key material, and decrypts v10/v11 records. Agent credentials, IDE vaults, cloud secret APIs and additional stores are also collected.
The same envelope and repository/HTTPS send chain exports results. Signed GitHub/GitLab search results reach eval(result.message), with signature verification implemented before acceptance.

jr() extracts an existing npm tarball, replaces its main entrypoint, writes native .node addons and an encrypted cache payload, overwrites postinstall, deletes earlier lifecycle entries, increments the patch version and repacks it. PyPI startup code construction accompanies package upload.

The embedded ELF N-API module registers init and reaches Run. Rizin disassembly shows cache-file read, XOR transformation, fork/setsid, temporary script write/chmod and execlp. Static XOR recovery with byte 0x96 yields a valid numeric/rotation-packed loader.

That loader authenticates/decrypts an AES-GCM/Brotli next stage and launches its source through Bun stdin. The next stage contains a self-source string plus an actual executing obfuscated runtime ending in CS(); it is another credential/propagation payload, not inert cached data.

A privileged Docker container specification binds host /etc/sudoers.d and writes the decoded passwordless runner grant. Other preflight paths disable a security runner or rewrite security-related networking. These are alternatives, not a claim all execute on every host.

Decoded monitor resources contain the same token-rejection home-wipe mechanism, session hooks and service registration as the first payload. The original hides the wipe command in its custom string cipher.
samples.benign_alternative: An ordinary cache helper or publisher has no reason to dump another process for secret records, export browser passwords, evaluate repository messages, or replace third-party package entrypoints with a native loader.
samples.missing_context: Original package name/version and installation host are unavailable. Shared implementation/resources establish a variant relationship; no actor attribution or unobserved compromise is asserted.
samples.coverage_limits: The original now has eight distinct hostile findings. Home-wipe configuration is encrypted in the original, so the new destructive-task matcher is confirmed on reconstructed source rather than falsely attributed to raw bytes. Full interprocedural flow exceeds the source analysis budget; co-occurrence composites are described as such.

samples.marker_line: sync-check workflow: Base32 leaks all Actions secrets to logs
execution_trace: On push, one Ubuntu job runs env | base32 -w 120 and echo -n toJSON(secrets) | base32 -w 120. Both pipelines write their encoded bytes to job stdout/logs.
Base32 changes the literal secret values before logging, bypassing verbatim secret masking. The source explicitly selects the complete Actions secrets object; no network callback is needed.
permissions:{} restricts workflow-token grants but does not remove repository secret context. The number/content of available secrets and readers of job logs depend on deployment.
samples.benign_alternative: Environment debugging can explain an environment dump. It does not justify encoding the complete secrets object into a build step with no build activity. A controlled canary test is possible but is not indicated by these bytes or supplied context.
samples.missing_context: Repository visibility, log readers, secret values and whether the workflow ran are unknown. No public-log or successful-theft claim is made.
samples.hostile_coverage_goal: One hostile and one suspicious finding accurately cover the supported secret-log leak and accompanying encoded environment dump. The two commands do not establish three to five distinct hostile techniques. Source and Base32-to-stdout legs were traced and the existing matchers verified; there is no additional supported hostile behavior to invent.
samples.classifier_disagreement: ML probability remains 0.97937423 with lvl=-1 and conf=0, i.e. no calibrated flag. The hostile rule fires and static behavior supports MALICIOUS. No duplicates/severity inflation were added to change that score.
